question: What does healthcare data access primarily mean for a clinical nurse?

options.A: The right to publish clinical research data online
options.B: The physical storage of paper case notes in a ward
options.C: The ability to retrieve and view patient information
options.D: The process of billing patients for hospital services

explanation: Data access refers directly to the retrieval and utilization of patient records by authorized personnel for care delivery. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h1)

question: Delayed access to patient health data most directly increases the risk of which outcome?

options.B: Immediate financial bankruptcy for the hospital
options.C: Automatic discharge of stable surgical patients
options.D: Immediate resignation of the attending physician

explanation: When clinical information is missing or delayed, nurses and doctors lack the complete picture, leading to potential mistakes in patient care. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h1)

question: Laboratory results and nursing care plans fall under which category of healthcare data?
explanation: Clinical data directly involves the medical and nursing care details, treatments, and diagnostic findings of the patient. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h2)

question: Electronic Health Records improve hospital workflow mainly by doing what?

options.A: Preventing patients from viewing their own medical history
options.B: Replacing the physical hospital bed with virtual monitoring
options.C: Allowing simultaneous access to patient details across departments
options.D: Eliminating the need for any nursing documentation at all

explanation: Digital records enable multiple healthcare workers in different units to view and update the same patient file at the same time. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h2)

question: Viewing a celebrity patient's electronic chart out of casual curiosity is an example of what?

options.A: A breach of privacy and confidentiality

explanation: Accessing medical records without a direct, legitimate clinical need to know violates patient privacy laws and professional ethics. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why do healthcare institutions act as custodians rather than owners of patient records?

options.A: Because hospitals are not allowed to store digital files
options.B: Because the physical data ultimately belongs to the patient
options.C: Because nurses take responsibility for hospital finances
options.D: Because government agencies own all private clinic computers

explanation: Patients retain fundamental ownership rights over their personal health information, while institutions merely manage and protect it. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h3)

question: Locking your computer workstation before walking away from the nurses' station is an example of what?
explanation: Securing physical access to hardware terminals prevents unauthorized individuals from viewing active patient screens. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of role-based access controls in an electronic health system?

options.A: Limiting staff access to only the data required for their specific job
options.B: Ensuring every hospital employee can view all patient records freely
options.C: Speeding up the internet connection speed in the children's ward
options.D: Reducing the overall cost of purchasing computer hardware

explanation: Role-based security ensures users only see files relevant to their specific clinical or administrative duties. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why is accurate nursing documentation essential within electronic health records?

options.A: Because computers automatically generate all vital signs
options.B: Because administrative staff write all clinical notes
options.C: Because hospital management requires daily poetry writing
options.D: Because nurses are primary generators of clinical data

explanation: Nurses directly input vital signs, care notes, and medication administration details, making their documentation the foundation of clinical data accuracy. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h5)

question: A nurse preparing to administer a new prescription in an emergency should check the electronic record first to confirm what crucial detail?

options.A: The current market price of the medication
options.B: Known drug allergies and medical history
options.C: The name of the hospital chief executive
options.D: The personal phone number of the pharmacist

explanation: Reviewing historical data for allergies prevents adverse drug reactions during acute interventions. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to healthcare data access in resource-limited settings?

options.A: Unlimited high-speed optical fiber in every room
options.B: Incomplete transition from paper to digital systems
options.C: Intermittent power supply and poor connectivity
options.D: Inadequate digital literacy training for staff

explanation: Unlimited high-speed infrastructure represents an ideal environment rather than a barrier, whereas power issues, lack of training, and paper reliance are actual hurdles. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h6)

question: How do incompatible software vendors negatively affect hospital information systems?

options.A: By forcing nurses to write all prescriptions using physical typewriters
options.B: By automatically deleting patient records every twenty-four hours
options.C: By lowering the financial cost of software maintenance licenses
options.D: By creating isolated silos of information that cannot easily share data

explanation: When different software platforms cannot talk to each other, patient data becomes trapped in separate departments, hampering continuity of care. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h6)
